text:
anya: Quick FYI — tundra-micro-int4 canary showing ~3.8% uptick in funcall parse failures vs float baseline, only on streaming paths. :thinking:

sam: Are we seeing full JSON corruption or schema mismatches?

anya: Mostly truncated suffixes and stray commas. Sampled 200 failures: ~70% missing closing brace, ~20% trailing commas.

lee: Example from logs (sanitized):
```
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "Login bug", "assignee": "ops",},
...stream cut...
```

maria: Sounds like streaming cutoff. Any tokenizer diffs between tundra-micro-int4 and baseline?

sam: Vocab unchanged, but PTQ can reorder logits for near-tied tokens -> EOS placement shifts. Could truncate output earlier.

lee: Also check continuous-batching and chunking config — longer tail tokens can be cut by the runtime chunker.

anya: For same prompt, float gave final tokens `..."}
` while int4 ended `...","` then stop — mid-JSON stop.

maria: CI-bot, run structured-output sanity on last 500 canary samples for int4 and baseline and post metrics.

ci-bot: Running structured-output-sanity (v2) on 500 samples for tundra-micro-int4. ETA ~2m.

sam: Infra, can you dump streaming chunk sizes and last-token logits for a few reproducer seeds? If highest-prob token flips, streaming heuristics may think EOS emitted.

lee: PTQ sometimes flips top-k ordering for ties. Our parser retries are rate-limited which could explain the spike.

anya: Short-term mitigation: opt-in "json-healer" for canary traffic that does minimal fixes (close braces, strip trailing commas) and flags repaired outputs. Keep raw output in logs. Thoughts?

maria: Prefer non-invasive postprocess that attempts minimal repair and marks healed_by_type (close_brace, strip_comma, pad_eos). Add dashboard tiles.

sam: Opt-in for canary only. Add metric healed_parse_success_rate.

lee: Also run a canary with kv-cache disabled to check if caching interaction amplifies truncation.

anya: Plan: (1) wait ci-bot results, (2) enable canary json-healer + metric, (3) kv-cache-off canary, (4) collect logits + chunk traces. I'll coordinate.

maria: I'll ship a tiny repair lib and a dashboard for healed metrics.

ci-bot: structured-output-sanity results: tundra-micro-int4: parse_success=92.1%, healed_success=3.6%, final_failure=4.3%. baseline: parse_success=96.0%, healed_success=0.5%, final_failure=3.5%. Full report uploaded to /canary/reports/tundra-micro-int4/1785001234.json

sam: Confirms regression ~3.9% relative. Healing helps but not sufficient.

lee: Run token-align: `token-align --compare tundra-micro-int4 baseline --samples 1000` and inspect diffs, focusing on punctuation/EOS.

anya: Kicked that off. If diffs cluster on punctuation/EOS tokens, PTQ tie flips likely.

maria: I'll queue a quick quant sweep (per-tensor vs per-channel calibrations, one additional clipping config) on the canary dataset. Could nudge borderline logits back.

sam: Release gate: hold broader rollout. Target: combined parse_success + healed_success >= baseline parse_success - 0.5%. Practically parse_success >=95.5% without heavy reliance on repair.

anya: Agreed. If sweep doesn't help, I'll open incident in #incidents and escalate. Thanks all :thumbsup:
